sectors.name: Technology
themes: AI infrastructure demand is a durable driver, with PLTR, ARM, and MRVL compounding on hyperscaler capex cycles that outlast rate cuts.
Indonesia's digital economy is entering a cloud-and-data-center buildout phase, making SLIS and IT structural beneficiaries of domestic AI adoption and government digitalization.
US-listed semiconductor and hardware names (ZBRA, COHR, ALAB) are riding a global supply-chain re-rating, but their cyclicality requires active rotation into software-led growth.
sectors.ai: Buy US-listed tech exposure via PLTR, ARM, and MRVL into AI-infrastructure strength; Indonesia's IDX tech (+0.79%) lags but SLIS (+26.98%) signals local AI-cloud momentum—rotate 15% of tech sleeve to SLIS and IT for domestic data-center capex. Trim ZBRA and COHR on profit-taking; hold ALAB for networking upside.

sectors.name: Financials
themes: Indonesia's digital finance sub-sector is decoupling from aggregate indices, rewarding niche players like DEFI and PEGE with outsized liquidity-driven rallies.
US fintech outperformance (HOOD, IVZ) is transmitting positive sentiment to IDX financials, but local names still trade at a valuation discount, supporting catch-up potential.
Regulatory clarity on micro-lending and payment infrastructure in Indonesia is a durable tailwind for smaller financials, favoring agile operators over conglomerates.
sectors.ai: Buy DEFI on momentum but rotate into PEGE and YULE for sustained beta; US fintech strength (HOOD, IVZ) confirms global risk-on, yet ID laggards (BEKS, SMIL) offer cheaper catch-up. Trim LPPS into strength; hold core exposure via diversified names.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's coal export demand remains structurally supported by Asian thermal power buildouts and domestic smelter mandates, sustaining volume growth for producers like BUMI and ALKA.
Nickel downstreaming policy—banning raw ore exports and pushing HPAL smelters—creates durable value-add margins for ANTM and BAJA, insulating them from commodity price swings.
US copper and steel names (FCX, NUE) benefit from electrification and infrastructure re-shoring, offering a hedge against IDX volatility while riding global energy transition capex.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian coal and nickel names on the WATCH signal, prioritizing ALKA and BAJA for momentum, but lock in partial profits given the 24.7% spike; add FCX for US copper leverage. Favor BUMI and ANTM as laggards with upside, avoid chasing EMAS. Rebalance into strength within 48 hours.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's nickel-to-battery vertical integration is creating a durable cost advantage for local EV and energy-storage players like TOBA, independent of global commodity price swings.
US solar and inverter makers (FSLR, ENPH, SEDG) benefit structurally from IRA-driven manufacturing reshoring and rising grid-scale demand, with margins improving as supply-chain bottlenecks ease.
Climate-tech capital is rotating toward profitable, cash-flow-positive operators over pre-revenue names, favoring firms with contracted backlogs and tariff-proof domestic production.
sectors.ai: Buy TOBA on the +14.75% breakout—Indonesia's EV/battery integration story is accelerating with domestic nickel downstreaming and policy tailwinds. Pair with US solar names (FSLR, ENPH) as rate-cut expectations and grid-demand data firm. Trim laggards, rotate into names with clear 2025 order books; avoid chasing PLUG's speculative hydrogen spike.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Indonesia's rising middle class and urbanization continue to drive premiumization in food, beverage, and personal care, supporting sustained volume growth for agile mid-cap FMCG players.
Digital distribution and direct-to-consumer channels are structurally expanding margins for consumer brands, enabling faster market penetration beyond traditional retail networks.
Consolidation among smaller consumer companies, via M&A or product-line expansion, is creating outsized re-rating opportunities as larger players seek scale in fragmented categories.
sectors.ai: Buy selective mid-cap consumer names showing momentum (ZONE, AGAR, WMPP) as the sector grinds higher on resilient domestic demand; rotate out of laggards into high-volume movers with earnings catalysts, but keep stops tight given NORMAL signal and mixed ID/US performance.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: US forwarders are structurally benefiting from supply-chain diversification and tariff-driven re-routing, creating durable demand for expedited and managed logistics services.
Indonesia's logistics sector is consolidating around integrated players (TRUK, BBRM) as e-commerce and downstream mineral processing drive higher-value, time-sensitive freight volumes.
Digital freight matching and AI-optimized routing are becoming margin differentiators, favoring asset-light operators (CHRW, EXPD) over legacy asset-heavy carriers.
sectors.ai: Logistics is turning constructive: US names (EXPD, CHRW, GTSI) are leading on peak-season freight demand and tariff front-running, while Indonesia's TRUK (+25%) signals domestic consolidation. Add selectively to US forwarders with pricing power and to ID trucking/port operators with volume visibility; trim pure-play ocean liners on rate volatility. Watch for Q3 earnings confirmation before full deployment.

Global programmatic ad tech, led by TTD, is gaining share as brands shift budgets to data-driven buying, a durable trend independent of local macro.

sectors.name: Property & Real Estate

Small-cap property stocks (EMDE, BKDP) are outperforming on retail investor rotation and low base effects, but liquidity risk remains high—favor names with proven execution.

Position ahead of Q3 presales data—expect double-digit growth in landed housing. Trim exposure to US-linked names; local liquidity favors small caps.
